activities.deviceNote: The live calculator does not add a separate end-user device term for everyday text prompts.
activities.label: AI text prompts
activities.note: Uses an everyday text-prompt estimate of about 0.3 Wh while keeping a separate prompt-specific water estimate of 0.26 mL direct and 1.3 mL total.

activities.deviceNote: The live calculator keeps the reasoning row equal to cloud-side energy until a separate prompt-device model is justified.
activities.label: High-reasoning prompts
activities.note: Uses the long high-reasoning 33.8 Wh benchmark rather than the much smaller medium-query comparison value, so this row stays an intentional outlier.

activities.deviceNote: No device, network, or facility-overhead add-on is available. The GPU-only benchmark is carried through both energy totals as a conservative floor, not as a measured full-system value.
activities.label: AI image generation
activities.note: Uses the IEA's 1.7 Wh SD-XL 1.0-base benchmark from controlled H100 testing. Jon Ippolito's What Uses More? comparison prompted the review; the adopted value comes from the underlying IEA report. The benchmark covers GPU electricity only and is carried through both energy columns as a conservative floor. Water remains an internal conversion rather than an image-specific measurement.
activities.serverEnergyBoundary: GPU electricity only; excludes network energy, facility overhead, and the end-user device.
activities.totalEnergyBoundary: Carries the 1.7 Wh GPU-only benchmark through as a conservative floor; this is not a measured total-system value.
activities.unitHint: One SD-XL 1.0-base image under controlled H100 test conditions

activities.deviceNote: Keep this fixed to a laptop-style coding session unless stronger desktop or thin-client evidence appears.
activities.label: Coding-agent use
activities.note: Uses the current one-hour coding-agent benchmark and adds a 30 Wh device allowance in the total-system column.
activities.unitHint: Hours of sustained agent use, not prompts

activities.deviceNote: This row already behaves like a mobile-default social-feed estimate and should stay fixed in the first device pass.
activities.label: TikTok or short-video scrolling
activities.note: Built from device-side social-video measurement plus streaming-style infrastructure assumptions; keep this row estimated until a platform-specific cloud-side benchmark exists.

activities.deviceNote: Keep Instagram locked to a phone-style total unless the row is split into cleaner photo versus video cases.
activities.label: Instagram scrolling
activities.note: This remains an analogy-based estimate built from social-media measurement plus streaming comparisons, useful for relative scale rather than platform accounting.

activities.deviceNote: Treat Snapchat as a phone-default row in the initial device model.
activities.label: Snapchat
activities.note: Another low-confidence social-media estimate built from broader comparison logic rather than a platform disclosure.

activities.deviceNote: The default total assumes phone viewing, while the stored laptop and TV options let the row reflect the much larger device spread behind video streaming.
activities.label: YouTube watching
activities.note: Uses the same CDN-style video benchmark as Netflix so the calculator keeps an apples-to-apples streaming anchor for the cloud-side and total-system columns.

activities.deviceNote: The default total assumes laptop viewing, while phone and TV options preserve the lower and higher ends already used in the scenario work.
activities.label: Netflix streaming
activities.note: Uses the IEA/Kamiya 22 Wh cloud-side and 77 Wh total benchmark used throughout the site's streaming comparisons.

activities.deviceNote: Keep this mixed-work row fixed to a laptop-style bundle until it is split into narrower activity rows.
activities.label: Email, cloud docs, and browsing
activities.note: This is a teaching bundle for light browsing, email, and cloud documents rather than a per-click benchmark.

activities.deviceNote: The current participant row assumes a laptop-style class session; add a phone option only when a clearer participant-device bridge is chosen.
activities.label: Zoom as participant
activities.note: Uses a one-hour participant meeting estimate in which network plus platform routing form the cloud-side figure and participant device energy is added back for the total-system column.

activities.deviceNote: This row is a shared meeting bundle, not a single host-device toggle, so keep it fixed.
activities.label: Zoom as host
activities.note: Uses a hosted Zoom estimate that counts all participant devices in the total-system column.

activities.deviceNote: Fixed to an Xbox Series X plus one reference 54.7-inch ENERGY STAR-certified television. Series S and alternate display choices are not yet modeled.
activities.directWaterBoundary: Modeled direct cooling and humidification water for the game-server data center only; telecom-facility water is unquantified.
activities.label: Gaming Console (Xbox Series X + TV)
activities.note: Locally rendered online multiplayer, not cloud gaming. The central estimate includes the console, reference TV, allocated home networking, fixed access and core transport, modeled game-server IT, and data-center overhead. Downloads, patches, manufacturing, standby, and optional texture streaming are excluded.
activities.serverEnergyBoundary: Off-prem fixed access and core transport plus modeled game-server facility electricity; excludes the allocated home gateway.
activities.totalEnergyBoundary: Console, reference TV, allocated home gateway, fixed access and core transport, modeled game-server IT, and PUE overhead for one player-hour.
activities.totalWaterBoundary: U.S.-average operational water consumption: electricity-generation water for quantified components plus modeled direct game-server data-center water.
activities.unitHint: One active player-hour; local rendering over fixed broadband
